title: SpaceX Starship Flight 15
dateText: 13 November 2026, 17:45 to 19:00 ET window (pending regulatory approval)
summary: SpaceX's Starship Flight 15 is set for 13 November 2026 from Starbase, Texas, with the first attempt to catch both the Super Heavy booster and the Starship upper stage. A double catch would open the way to the first reflight of a recovered ship.
stakes: SpaceX has confirmed a 13 November 2026 target, with a 75 minute window opening at 17:45 ET, pending regulatory approval; the date had earlier moved from 8 November to 12 November and then 13 November.

SpaceX plans to catch both stages with the launch tower's arms; a success would be the first full recovery of a Starship vehicle and would allow the first reflight of a properly recovered ship (NASASpaceflight).
Elon Musk put the chance of a successful ship catch on the first attempt at about 50 to 60 percent (Space Launch Schedule, Wikipedia).
Flight 14 on 28 September 2026 was the first Starship flight to reach orbit and deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites, though the booster and the ship each lost an engine during ascent.

Booster 22 completed a 16-second, full-duration static fire of all 33 engines on 25 October 2026 (Aviation Week), and both the booster and Ship 42 had completed static fire testing by 27 October (WAI Hub).
Flight 16, targeted for December, could be the first Starship launch from Launch Complex 39A in Florida; NASASpaceflight notes those plans depend on how Flight 15 goes.
facts: Booster catch about 6.5 minutes after liftoff; payload deploy in orbit; ship catch at Starbase about 22.5 hours after liftoff (SpaceX)

title: AST SpaceMobile BlueBirds 14, 15 and 16 Launch
vehicle: Falcon 9 (listed by launch trackers; AST has not announced the launch)
dateText: Fourth quarter 2026 (no date announced; launch trackers list no earlier than 30 December)
summary: AST SpaceMobile's BlueBirds 14, 15 and 16 reached Cape Canaveral in October 2026 and await a launch date, listed for the fourth quarter. The launch would take the constellation to 16 satellites as AST works towards about 45 in orbit by early 2027.
stakes: AST is aiming for about 45 satellites in orbit by early 2027 and about 90 for continuous global coverage; BlueBirds 11 to 13 took the count to 13 in August 2026.

In October 2026 AST said it was targeting initial, intermittent coverage by the end of 2026 in the US, Canada, Japan, the UK and Saudi Arabia, with more satellites extending how long and how often coverage is available (Light Reading).
AST's full year 2026 revenue guidance is $150 million to $200 million, with about half expected to come from contracted backlog.
Advanced Television reports this batch is about a month behind the schedule shown in August, and that later launches depend partly on the availability of Blue Origin's New Glenn.
Space Launch Schedule and Orbital Radar list the Falcon 9 launch for no earlier than 30 December 2026 (Pacific time), a placeholder at the end of the quarter rather than a confirmed date.
AST reports third quarter 2026 results on 9 November 2026 after the market closes, which may bring a firmer launch date (Barchart).

title: Firefly Alpha Block 2 First Launch (Flight 8)
dateText: Fourth quarter 2026 (launch trackers list no earlier than 30 December)
summary: Firefly Aerospace is targeting the fourth quarter of 2026 for Alpha Flight 8 from Vandenberg, the first flight of the upgraded Alpha Block 2. It is one of two more Alpha launches Firefly plans this year and the first test of the reliability upgrades in flight.
stakes: Firefly said on its second quarter 2026 call that it is targeting Flights 8 and 9 this year, for three Alpha launches in 2026.
Block 2 is an upgrade intended to improve Alpha's reliability; Block 2 avionics flew in shadow mode on Flight 7 in March 2026.
Before launch the rocket still needs acceptance testing, delivery to Vandenberg, a static fire and payload integration.
Firefly says most of its 2027 Alpha manifest is already sold.

Launch tracker Orbital Radar lists Flight 8 from SLC-2W no earlier than 30 December 2026 (Pacific time), carrying the TacSat technology demonstration satellite; Firefly has not announced a date and reports third quarter results on 10 November 2026.

title: Intuitive Machines IM-3 Moon Landing Mission
dateText: First quarter of 2027 (launch window January to March)
summary: Intuitive Machines' IM-3 lunar lander is scheduled to launch on a Falcon 9 in a January to March 2027 window, aiming for the Reiner Gamma region of the Moon. It is the company's third landing attempt, after IM-2 ended with its lander on its side in March 2025.
stakes: On the second quarter 2026 call, management said IM-3 was in assembly, integration and test, with an engine test still to come before a final green light to fly in the first quarter of 2027.
IM-3 flies under a NASA Commercial Lunar Payload Services task order (CP-11) and carries Lunar Vertex, NASA's CADRE rovers and instruments from ESA and Korea's KASI.
Intuitive Machines reported record second quarter 2026 revenue of $206 million and backlog of $1.8 billion, and kept its full-year revenue outlook of $900 million to $1 billion.
The company said IM-4 remains planned for late 2027.

title: Virgin Galactic Delta Spaceship Apeiron Flight Tests
vehicle: Delta-class spaceship Apeiron, carried by VMS Eve
dateText: Flight tests after avionics software validation; first commercial spaceflight expected early second quarter 2027
summary: Virgin Galactic flew its first Delta-class spaceship, Apeiron, to Spaceport America on 28 October 2026 ahead of captive carry, glide and powered test flights. First commercial service is now expected in early Q2 2027, the flights meant to return the company to revenue.
stakes: On 26 October 2026 Virgin Galactic moved its first Delta commercial spaceflight from February 2027 to early in the second quarter of 2027, citing extra time for avionics software integration and validation (Yahoo Finance).

The shares fell about 2% after hours on the announcement (Yahoo Finance); an earlier delay in August, from the fourth quarter of 2026 to February 2027, was followed by a fall of about 13% after hours (TechTimes).
A second Delta ship is expected to enter service in late Q2 or early Q3 2027, with two-ship commercial operations targeted for early Q3 2027 (Yahoo Finance).
Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities were $286 million at 30 June 2026.

title: Telesat Lightspeed First Satellites Launch
dateText: Around June 2027 (Telesat: rideshare on a third-party Falcon 9 in mid-2027)
summary: Telesat's first two Lightspeed satellites, built by MDA Space, will now ride on a third-party Falcon 9 around June 2027 rather than in December 2026. The slip pushes global Lightspeed service back to the end of the second quarter of 2028.
stakes: On its third quarter 2026 call, Telesat said it would not use one of its own Falcon 9 slots for two satellites and will instead ride on a third-party Falcon 9 in mid-2027; after about two months of in-orbit testing it will start launching 15 satellites per Falcon 9 (Via Satellite).

Global service moves from the end of the first quarter to the end of the second quarter of 2028, while Telesat says service in higher latitudes, including for the Canadian military in the Arctic, still starts by the end of the first quarter of 2028 (Via Satellite).
Telesat reported a Lightspeed contractual backlog of $5.6 billion and, in August 2026, signed a $2.7 billion polar satellite communications contract with Canada's Defence Investment Agency (SpaceQ).
MDA Space builds the Lightspeed satellites; an August 2026 order for 27 more took its total to 225 and added $474 million to the contract value (MDA Space).
Lightspeed is meant to offset declines in Telesat's geostationary business (SpaceNews).
Telesat reported CA$3.1 billion of GEO debt maturing between December 2026 and October 2027 and is seeking to refinance it (Via Satellite).
facts: Third-party Falcon 9 rideshare (pathfinders); 15 satellites per Falcon 9 for the main campaign
Higher latitudes by the end of Q1 2028; global service by the end of Q2 2028

title: Globalstar HIBLEO-4 Replacement Satellites: Second Launch
summary: Globalstar's second set of MDA Space-built HIBLEO-4 replacement satellites is due to launch on a Falcon 9 in a December 2026 window. Completing the replenishment matters because certain HIBLEO-4 milestones are a condition of Globalstar's pending sale to Amazon.
stakes: Globalstar says the pending Amazon transaction is expected to close in 2027 and remains subject to closing conditions including outstanding regulatory approvals and Globalstar's achievement of certain HIBLEO-4 satellite milestones (third quarter 2026 results).

The replacement satellites support the reliability and continuity of Globalstar's existing mobile satellite services network; the FCC Space Bureau approved Amazon's application to acquire Globalstar's FCC licences in October 2026.
By 30 September 2026 Globalstar had incurred $303.2 million with MDA Space and $121.4 million with SpaceX for milestones on the replacement satellites (10-Q).
Third quarter 2026 revenue was $70.9 million, about 4% lower than a year earlier (TradingView 10-Q summary).
